feature: ordinary gRPC Channel outlier detection completion ownership

terminal_sources: parsed OK and non-OK gRPC status
scope.lifetime: returned streaming handles retain completion only while their owning ordinary Channel and slot remain valid, matching the existing Channel lifetime contract

reference.implementation: grpc-core C++ outlier detection picker SubchannelCallTracker
reference.observed_contract: one tracker is attached to each completed child pick and records status exactly once when that physical call finishes

implementation.observer: ClientWriter and ClientDuplex carry one nullable pointer; an observer allocation occurs only when ordinary Channel has an enabled outlier policy
implementation.exactly_once: terminal, reset, cancellation, fatal error, and deinit clear the pointer before invoking and destroying the observer
implementation.unary: unary attempts record immediately before retry policy decides whether to replay
implementation.resolver: matched DNS slots move their detector state with the live connection; new addresses start with clean buckets
implementation.selection: round-robin, weighted selection, connection racing, ready probes, and fail-fast checks exclude ejected slots without closing their transport
implementation.timing: wait-for-ready includes the next evaluation deadline and later calls lazily evaluate before picking an idle ordinary Channel

native_cases: ordinary unary endpoint A returns UNAVAILABLE and is ejected before B is connected
two calls during ejection use B and the first post-duration call returns to A
sequential ClientWriter UNAVAILABLE terminal drives fail-fast ConnectionUnavailable and aggregate TRANSIENT_FAILURE
ClientDuplex UNAVAILABLE terminal drives the same transition
ordinary and Shared detectors share success-rate, failure-percentage, max-percent, multiplier, and unejection evaluator coverage

results.external_boundary: grpc-cpp is a transport and picker regression gate; deterministic ordinary outlier behavior is proven by native real-endpoint tests
